newsitem.title: USA: Former IRA member granted political asylum in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Former IRA member granted political asylum in U.S..

text.p: An U.S. immigration judge on Thursday granted political asylum to a former Irish Republican Army member who was released from a prison nine years ago for bombing British barracks in 1975.
The judge denied deportation of Brian Pearson, 45, who has lived in the United States since 1988, is married to an American citizen and has a 5-year-old daughter.
The U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service had sought to deport Pearson because of his role in the bombing.
Immigration Judge Phillip Williams said in his ruling that Pearson, a carpenter, has led an "exemplary life" while in the United States and has not been involved in any criminal activity.
Williams also found that Pearson had established a "well founded fear of persecution" if he were to be returned to Britain.
"The court finds that the respondent is eligible and deserving of a grant of political asylum," Williams said.
Pearson was convicted in 1977 of participating in two 1975 bombings. He testified that he was brutally tortured while in prison. After his release in 1988, he immigrated to the United States.
Pearson testified that he would fear for his life and the lives of his family if he were returned to any part of Ireland. He said he is afraid of the British Army and loyalists paramilitary groups.
"He testified that he believes that this will happen because he is a known ex-political prisoner and he supports Sinn Fein and unification of Ireland," the judge said.
